tools.name: researcher_capture_wiki
tools.description: Capture one explicitly named retained wiki revision as immutable exact-quotation evidence. Reading/editing a wiki does not itself create a source. Read the resulting captured source before citing. The snapshot may intentionally be historical; it does not prove current-page state or scientific validity. Reuse operation_key after a lost receipt.

tools.name: researcher_capture_wiki_collection
tools.description: Capture all 1–50 explicitly selected wiki revisions into a bounded normalized source, preserving member offsets/hashes. Use researcher_source_query for offline paraphrase recovery and source_structure for exact member locators. This covers only selected members, never an unlisted whole wiki. Excess size/empty/foreign/duplicate members fail without partial capture. Reuse operation_key; no hidden model/vector store is used.

items.description: One explicit authorized project/global revision in a bounded wiki corpus.

tools.name: researcher_wiki_list
tools.description: List one explicit wiki namespace with stable next_after_id; optional query is lexical FTS, not semantic absence evidence. Never merge global pages implicitly. Use a captured explicit revision collection and researcher_source_query for paraphrases. Metadata is contextual documentation, not scientific validation.

tools.name: researcher_wiki_read
tools.description: Read the exact stored logical path in one namespace, with id/revision/hash and next_offset. Read all required windows before editing; retain page_id, revision and full title/body/parent state. This read does not create a citable source. Global misses never fall back to a project or vice versa.

tools.name: researcher_wiki_write
tools.description: Write only this project's wiki, with stable operation_key. Creation uses expected_revision0 and page_id null. Editing requires the exact observed page_id/revision and complete title/body/parent state; null parent clears it. A stale or recreated page conflicts; do not rebase/overwrite silently. Preserve the draft and compare first. A wiki edit is context, not task acceptance, scientific validation or publication.
